title: Homage to Savitṛ, the one eye of the world

words.meaning: to the one eye of the world
to the cause of the world’s birth, continuance and destruction
to the one made of the three Vedas
to the one who bears the three guṇas as his self
to the one whose self is Viriñci (Brahmā), Nārāyaṇa and Śaṅkara

samasa.meaning: the one eye of the world

samasa.vigraha: जगतः प्रसूतेः स्थितेः नाशस्य च हेतुः
samasa.meaning: the cause of the world’s birth, existence and destruction

samasa.vigraha: विरिञ्चिः नारायणः शङ्करः च आत्मा यस्य सः
samasa.meaning: whose self is Brahmā, Nārāyaṇa and Śaṅkara

morphology.note: trayī ‘the triad’ is the three Vedas; -maya ‘made of, consisting of’.

translation.literal: Homage to Savitṛ, the one eye of the world, the cause of the world’s birth, continuance and destruction, made of the three Vedas, bearing the three guṇas as his self, whose self is Viriñci, Nārāyaṇa and Śaṅkara.
translation.readable: Homage to Savitṛ, the world’s single eye, by whom the world is born, sustained and dissolved; who is the three Vedas, who holds the three guṇas, and who is Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva in one.

meaning: The first of four verses to the Sun as Nārāyaṇa at the close of the rite. It gathers the Sun into one figure who is everything the rite has addressed: the eye by which the world is seen, the cause of its arising, lasting and passing away, the substance of the three Vedas, the bearer of the three guṇas, and Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva together — the same three that the dhyāna verses of the japa assigned to the morning, the evening and midday.
in_the_rite: Step sūrya-nārāyaṇa-vandana, all three services, facing east (S marks the direction).
